prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an indoor room bordered by a windowed wall on the left that recedes from roughly 1.5 m in the foreground to over 5 m in the dark background, with a bright clothing rack positioned in front and to the left at about 0.5–1.5 m from the camera wearer. A man in a plaid shirt stands to the right of the rack at roughly 1.2–1.5 m in frames 1 and 3 (facing left and angled slightly toward the camera wearer while looking down at the rack rather than at the camera wearer), while two background people in frame 1 appear as faint silhouettes 3–5 m away behind the rack and about 1–1.5 m apart from each other. In frame 2, as the camera tilts down and left, a bright arm and torso at the far left edge (about 0.8 m away) and the camera wearer's hand at the bottom edge (within 0.4 m) are separated by about 0.8 m from the bright hanging clothes on the right (0.6–1.0 m), which largely occlude the plaid-shirted man behind them at the right edge. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer approaches to within 0.4–0.8 m of both the rack and the plaid-shirted man on the right, bringing the top bar, hangers, and the man's extended right arm into bright near-field range within arm's reach of both people, alongside the camera wearer's own hand entering at the bottom-left of frame 5 (~0.3 m). Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the foreground rack and reaching arm from the mid-ground torso and distant wall, though it is unreliable on the window glass (which appears black/infinite despite exterior objects) and merges the hanging garments into a smooth, featureless blob that obscures individual hangers.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates people and foreground objects against a black background across the five frames, placing the plaid-shirted man on the right at roughly 1.2–1.5 m in frames 1 and 3 and 0.4–0.8 m as the camera wearer approaches in frames 4 and 5, with his head angled left and downward toward the rack rather than looking at the camera wearer. In frame 1, it detects the two distant people behind the rack on the left at 3–5 m (spaced ~1–1.5 m apart and partially occluded by the rack), making them much easier to spot than in the motion-blurred RGB image, and also labels the person on the far-left edge of frame 2 (~0.8 m away, ~0.8 m left of the rack). However, the map is highly unreliable on the clothing rack within arm's reach (0.4–1.2 m away on the left): it completely misses the rack in frame 1, misclassifies the hanging garments as a 'person' in frame 2 (merging them with the occluded man on the right) and as a green 'backpack' in frame 3, and falsely labels the shirts in the lower-left of frames 4 and 5 as part of a 'person' mask. Additionally, in frame 5 the mask for the close-up man on the right fragments and leaks onto the rack while his upper head and lower torso remain cropped out of view, failing to separate the garments being touched from the people.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map renders 2D body (yellow) and hand (magenta) keypoints on a black background, showing the plaid-shirted man on the right in frames 1 and 3 at ~1.2–1.5 m with his torso angled toward the camera wearer, his facial keypoints turned left and downward toward the clothing rack (not looking at the camera wearer), and his right hand extended within arm's reach to touch the garments on the left while his left hand hangs near his hip at the bottom edge of frame 1. It makes the exact finger articulation of his reaching right hand in frames 1, 4, and 5 much clearer than in the dark, motion-blurred RGB frames as the camera wearer moves from ~1.5 m in frame 1 to within ~0.5 m of the rack in frames 4 and 5. However, the pose estimator is completely missing all skeletons in frame 2 (failing on both the partially visible person at ~0.8 m on the left edge and the occluded man behind the clothes on the right) and fails to detect the two distant background people 3–5 m away in frame 1 or the camera wearer's own hand entering at ~0.3 m in the bottom-left of frame 5. Furthermore, in frames 3, 4, and 5, where the plaid-shirted man's lower body and parts of his head are cropped out of the frame, the body skeleton is severely distorted: it shrinks his torso into a miniature full-body figure in frame 3 and hallucinates horizontal leg keypoints stretching rightward across his chest and shoulder in frames 4 and 5 around his accurately localized magenta hand.
